description:
Make repository-local artifact layout an issue-based directory convention that the archival mechanism can actually service, and clean up the development root that the current flat-file layout has accumulated.

## Background

Two coupled defects surfaced as advisory findings against the repository-state quality-hardening epic's independent holistic review, and one of them cost a hand-repaired `jit validate` failure during that epic's own execution.

**The archival mechanism cannot service a whole class of artifact.** `jit archive document|container` refuses any selected root that is neither managed, permanent, nor already archived (`crates/jit/src/domain/artifact_classifier.rs:838-850`). This repository's development root has twelve areas; the shipped `managed_paths` default names three (`dev/active`, `dev/studies`, `dev/sessions`). `dev/presentations` is absent, so archiving the predecessor showcase deck had to be hand-rolled with `git mv`. That bypass skipped the planner's `reference_changes` remapping, the predecessor epic's document reference dangled, and `jit validate` hard-failed until the reference was repointed by hand. Previewing `jit archive container 1cc809de` reproduces the gap against the hardening epic's own artifacts: `eligible: false`, with `unmanaged-selected-root` blockers for the architecture document, the successor deck, and the tombstone.

Classifying areas needs care in both directions. `dev/architecture` holds living contributor documentation yet is linked to a Done issue, so making it *managed* would move it out from under readers on the next container archive; it belongs in `permanent_paths`, which archives by copy and retains the source.

**The flat layout does not scale and the archive shape disagrees with itself.** 172 artifacts across `dev/active` and `dev/archive` are named `<short-id>-<artifact>.md` at area root. Most of `dev/active` is owned by terminal issues and should have been archived long ago. Meanwhile `dev/archive` mixes the planner's `<short-id>-<slug>/` output with hand-made `features/`, `bug-fixes/`, `refactorings/`, `sessions/` and `studies/` subdirectories, and the planner's title-derived slug fallback produces names truncated mid-word — `dev/archive/a9b5dd08-use-strategic-label-slugs-in-archive-directory-n/` is its own counter-example.

Directory-per-issue precedents already exist in the repository: `dev/presentations/<short-id>/`, `dev/archive/features/<short-id>/`, and the planner's own `<short-id>-<slug>/`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A freshly initialized repository classifies every area under the development root as either managed or permanent, with `dev/presentations` managed and `dev/architecture` permanent, and reports a configured documentation policy without any hand-editing of its configuration. The classification is derived from initialization code and templates rather than from this repository's live `.jit/` contents.
- [hard] REQ-02: `jit archive document` and `jit archive container` produce an eligible plan for a presentation deck owned by a terminal issue; no `unmanaged-selected-root` blocker is reported for a configured development area.
- [hard] REQ-03: An issue's canonical artifact directory is `<area>/<short-id>-<slug>` when the issue carries a membership label, and `<area>/<short-id>` otherwise. No directory name is derived from an issue title.
- [hard] REQ-04: A command resolves an issue's canonical artifact directory, and tooling and documentation obtain the path from that command rather than composing it from a spelled-out pattern.
- [hard] REQ-05: Artifact filenames inside an issue directory carry no short-id prefix.
- [hard] REQ-06: An advisory report lists every artifact under a managed issue-scoped area that sits outside its owning issue's canonical directory. The report blocks no state transition.
- [hard] REQ-07: The archival planner derives an archive directory name from a membership label or a bare short id with no title fallback, and every pre-existing title-slugged archive directory is renamed with its container marker still resolving the renamed directory.
- [hard] REQ-08: An archival plan reports, as plan warnings, every occurrence of a moving artifact's path in the text of a file in the configured scan universe, including occurrences in code comments and shell scripts, and reports them identically whether or not the repository is under version control. Execution rewrites no document content.
- [hard] REQ-09: Every `dev/active` artifact owned by a terminal issue outside this epic's own subtree is archived through `jit archive container --execute`, and afterwards `jit validate` passes with every document reference in the repository resolving.
- [hard] REQ-10: Every artifact in `dev/active`, `dev/studies`, and `dev/sessions` that carries no issue prefix has a recorded disposition — an assigned owning issue, a project-scoped reclassification, or an archived location — and none is left undecided.
- [hard] REQ-11: Every agent skill prompt and reference template under `.agents/skills` that reads or writes an issue artifact path obtains it from the convention rather than from a hard-coded flat `dev/active/<short-id>-<artifact>` path, and every edited file that is a declared profile asset carries identical content in its packaged twin.
- [hard] REQ-12: Adopter-facing documentation states the directory convention and the area classification once, in a single canonical home.
- [hard] REQ-13: Pre-existing flat artifacts remain resolvable: the convention change and the cleanup together break no document reference, and legacy layouts are tolerated rather than restructured in place.
- [hard] REQ-14: No `unmanaged-selected-root` blocker is reported for a document linked at a source, script, agent-asset, or repository-root path, and executing a plan that contains such an artifact relocates no file outside the development root.
- [hard] REQ-15: A link target that resolves to a directory is treated as navigation rather than as an artifact: it produces no `unsupported-artifact-type` blocker, and a container whose remaining blockers were all directory targets yields an eligible plan.

## Decisions

- D-1: The convention is `<area>/<short-id>-<slug>` with the slug drawn only from a membership label, falling back to a bare `<short-id>` directory. Title-derived slugs are rejected because they yield long names truncated mid-word.
- D-2: Artifact filenames inside an issue directory drop the redundant short id, matching the existing `dev/archive/features/25064508/` shape.
- D-3: The issue-scoped areas that adopt the directory convention are `dev/active`, `dev/studies`, `dev/plans`, and `dev/presentations`. `dev/architecture`, `dev/design`, `dev/sessions`, `dev/experiments`, `dev/eval`, `dev/benchmarks`, and `dev/vision` stay flat. Adoption is independent of archival classification: a managed area that stays flat still archives its linked artifacts, and only the naming differs.
- D-4: The convention governs newly created artifacts. Pre-existing flat files are tolerated rather than restructured in place, mirroring the planner's existing adoption of a legacy archive directory without data movement.
- D-5: The change lands as a shipped product default, and this repository then adopts it. The dogfooding boundary applies: shipped behaviour comes from initialization code and templates.
- D-6: Archival policy is fixed by classifying each development area explicitly rather than by a blanket rule over the development root, so a living-documentation area is never swept into move-on-archive.
- D-7: Enforcement is a resolver command plus an advisory report. No blocking validation rule, because legacy flat artifacts are deliberately tolerated and a cutover predicate would be a false-positive source.
- D-8: Archival planning warns about in-content citation breakage and never rewrites document content, because a citation inside a dated historical document must survive verbatim.
- D-9: The planner's `<short-id>-<slug>/` shape is the canonical archive shape. The hand-made semantic subdirectories under `dev/archive` remain as legacy and are not migrated.
- D-10: The cleanup runs through `jit archive container --execute` rather than by hand, so the repaired mechanism's reference remapping is exercised on real artifacts and the run is itself acceptance evidence.
- D-11: Agent skill prompts in this repository are in scope, and each edited file's packaged profile-asset twin travels with it in the same change. Deferring the twins was rejected: they are asserted byte-equal to their source-tree originals, so a root-only edit fails the test suite outright. Restricting the criterion to files that are not declared assets was also rejected, because that excludes nearly every skill document and would leave the shipped skills carrying the flat path.
- D-12: The epic ships in milestone v1.0 and blocks the release: an adopter cannot archive a whole artifact class through the supported workflow, and shipped-default changes are cheaper before adopters exist.
- D-13: Managed areas are `dev/active`, `dev/studies`, `dev/sessions`, `dev/plans`, `dev/presentations`, `dev/design`, `dev/benchmarks`, and `dev/experiments`; permanent areas are `dev/architecture`, `dev/eval`, and `dev/vision`, plus the three development-root files `dev/index.md`, `dev/TESTING.md`, and `dev/authoring-conventions.md` declared as explicit file entries. `dev/vision` is permanent because `dev/vision/9db27a3a-charter.md` is a configured item-kind source and archiving the v1.0 milestone would move it out from under that configuration. `dev/eval` is permanent because its harnesses' invocation paths are documented commands. `dev/design`, `dev/benchmarks`, and `dev/experiments` are managed because their contents are revision-specific work products of terminal issues, and the benchmark generator recreates its output directory on the next run. A bare `dev/` permanent entry was rejected: classification matches by path prefix, so it would make every managed area permanent and silently defeat move-on-archive.
- D-14: A linked artifact outside the development root is retained where it is: no destination is scheduled for it and its source is untouched. Artifact discovery stops following links at such an artifact rather than walking through it. Source code, scripts, agent assets, and repository-root files are never relocated by an archive, and no unmanaged-selected-root blocker is reported for them. Classifying them permanent so they archive by copy was implemented first and then rejected on measurement: permanence sets keep-the-source while leaving wants-a-destination true, so copying fell out as an inherited consequence rather than a chosen behaviour, and because discovery walks an unbounded transitive link closure through the densely cross-linked adopter documentation set, this repository's 24 terminal containers scheduled 684 copy operations over 139 distinct files and 16.6 MB of duplicated content, including seven frozen mirrors of the whole adopter documentation tree, which `@/invariant/single-source-prose` and `@/charter/D-13` both name as a staleness defect. A relative or root-relative citation of a retained artifact no longer resolves from the archived side, because the citing document moves or is copied under the archive root while its target stays put; the execution-time layout validator therefore exempts an edge whose target is retained outside the development root, since demanding such an edge stay reachable would forbid relocating anything that cites one. Only a relative reference is at risk: it is interpreted from the citing document's own directory, so relocating the document changes what it names. A root-relative reference is interpreted from the repository root, which archival never moves, so it survives relocation intact. Measured over this repository's 24 terminal containers that is 11 citations, all relative: 9 sit on copied parents whose live originals keep resolving, so only the frozen snapshot is affected, and 2 sit on one relocated document and are dead everywhere. The 2 are rewritten before their container archives rather than accepted. Unlinking the affected documents was rejected because it destroys the traceability from ten terminal issues to the artifacts they delivered; folding the change into REQ-01 and REQ-02 was rejected because both scope themselves to a development area and the added scope would be invisible to review.

- D-15: The REQ-10 disposition is per-file for the artifacts in `dev/active` that carry no issue prefix, and one recorded blanket reclassification each for the unprefixed artifacts of `dev/sessions` and `dev/studies`. The `dev/studies/perf/` subtree is carved out of the blanket call and retained where it is, because a committed self-test script reads one of its measurement records at runtime. Per-file across all three areas was rejected as volume without added signal over two areas of uniformly dated records; a blanket call over all three was rejected because it would sweep genuinely issue-owned `dev/active` design documents into a project-scoped bucket without inspection.
- D-16: The REQ-08 citation scan matches any occurrence of a moving artifact's path in the text of a file in its scan universe, which is a configured set of repository-relative roots defaulting to the development root together with the permanent paths. Deriving the universe from version-control tracking was rejected because archival is a core command and core commands do not require git (`@/charter/D-4`), so a tracking-derived warning set would silently empty in a repository with no version control. Matching only markdown link targets was rejected because it reaches 2 of the 26 measured citations and misses every shell-script line, the production module doc comment, and both adopter-facing citations, all of which are inline code spans. A universe fixed to the development root was rejected because the adopter-facing and executable citations live outside it, so the default reaches the permanent paths and the configuration can widen it further.
- D-17: The REQ-14 relaxation is scoped to artifacts outside the configured development root, rather than to any artifact matching no configured area. A blanket relaxation was rejected because it would turn a mistyped managed-path entry into silent copying with no diagnostic, discarding the very signal the blocker exists to raise. Enumerating each outside root as permanent was rejected as a maintenance treadmill that re-blocks on the first unlisted root, and prefix matching would make an entry such as the crate source root permanent wholesale.
- D-18: A link target that resolves to a directory is navigation rather than a document, and artifact discovery skips it. Rewriting this repository's directory links was rejected because they are legitimate markdown and the defect would stay shipped for every adopter; narrowing the cleanup criterion was rejected because it would leave the epic's own acceptance evidence partial and the defect unrecorded.
- D-19: The area classification reaches the repository-initialization scaffold, so a freshly initialized repository reports a configured documentation policy. Shipping it only in the runtime accessor defaults was rejected because policy status ignores those defaults, which satisfies the classification criterion's letter while leaving the archival criterion unreachable. Making policy status honour accessor defaults was rejected as changing archive eligibility for every existing repository that has no explicit documentation table.

- D-20: The repository cleanup decomposes to one issue per container archival execution, and those issues carry whole-repository validation as their only gate. One issue per execution is what makes whole-sweep coverage answerable from the dependency graph rather than from a worker's summary. Grouping executions into thematic batches was rejected because a batch hides which executions actually ran. An adversarial per-issue review on these issues was rejected as disproportionate: each one runs a single pre-enumerated command over a footprint fixed at planning time, so the meaningful check is that the repository still validates afterwards. The same reasoning applies to the disposition issues, whose per-file outcomes are decided at planning time and executed without judgement.

- D-21: A task's declared footprint names the paths it mutates. For an archival execution that is the destination it creates plus the sources the plan moves; a source the plan copies is retained and is a read-only input, recorded in the issue body rather than the footprint. Declaring read-only inputs as footprint entries was rejected because it reports a task that writes one destination as touching every artifact its container ever produced, which makes the overlap advisories unreadable and hides the real write conflicts among them.

## Non-goals

- Restructuring pre-existing flat artifacts into issue directories in place.
- Migrating the hand-made `dev/archive` semantic subdirectories into the planner shape.
- Automatic rewriting of in-content path citations.
- A blocking validation rule for convention conformance.
- The `VirtualPath` composite-path API and the `InMemoryStorage::issue_vpath` panic path, both recorded as follow-ups elsewhere.

## Notes

Cross-cutting constraints: `@/inv/single-source-prose`, `@/inv/derived-state-coherence`, `@/charter/D-13`, `@/charter/D-14`, `@/charter/D-3`.

Evidence for the two defects is recorded in the predecessor epic's completion report at `dev/archive/1cc809de-completion-report.md`, whose holistic-review advisory findings F1 and F2 name them, and in the `dev/archive/a9b5dd08-use-strategic-label-slugs-in-archive-directory-n/` directory name.

REQ-09 is scoped to terminal issues outside this epic's own subtree because the epic cannot archive its own working artifacts while it executes them. Its plan, breakdown manifest and per-issue evidence records are owned by terminal children — the planning node and closed tasks — yet sit in no archived container's dependency closure, since the container that would relocate them is this epic. Archiving them mid-execution would remove the records the remaining waves consume; unlinking them would destroy the traceability `@/issue/8e071e18/decision/D-14` rejected unlinking for. They archive when the epic itself is archived. The set grows as children close, which is why the scope is stated structurally rather than as an enumerated exception list. Owner-approved amendment.
title: Issue-based development artifact layout and serviceable archival
